question: As global trade increases, many goods including those we use on daily basis are produced in another country and have to be transported long distances . Do benefits of this trend outweigh disadvantages
essay:
With the increase in global trade, many goods, including everyday commodities, are manufactured overseas and have to be transported across considerable distances. Although this trend has some undeniable drawbacks, I believe the advantages outweigh them because international trade gives consumers access to a wider range of products, often at affordable prices, and allows countries to specialise in goods they can produce efficiently.

On the one hand, international trade allows people to access a wider variety of goods and provides them with a wider range of choices. Consumers can purchase the goods that are not manufactured domestically, often at competitive prices. As countries can specialise in producing particular goods they can manufacture efficiently, these products can be transported to different countries. For example, countries with an efficient electronics industry can export smartphones, computers, and laptops to other countries. As a result, consumers can access a greater variety of electronics at different prices.

On the other hand, transportation over long distances can also contribute to severe environmental consequences and delays in the supply of products. International trade can also cause serious damage to the environment by shipping goods over long distances. For example, aeroplanes, ships, and trains consume large amounts of fuel and produce greenhouse gas emissions, leading to global warming. Additionally, when transportation is disrupted by natural disasters, conflicts, or logistical problems, businesses may not receive their products on time, which can cause delays in the supply of goods.

In conclusion, although international trade can contribute to environmental issues and delays, its benefits outweigh the disadvantages because it offers access to a wider range of products that are not manufactured domestically, while allowing different nations to specialise in goods they can produce effectively.

question: In many countries people are having their first child at a much later age than previous generations did. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this development.
essay:
In many countries of the world, the people are becoming parents much later than before. In the past, the women had their first baby when they were around twenty years old, but nowadays it is common to wait until thirty or more. This development has both the advantages and the disadvantages.

There are several advantages of having the children later. Firstly, the parents are more mature and they have more experience of the life, so they can take better decisions for their child. Secondly, they are usually more stable in the financial way. They have finished their education and they have a good job, so they can provide everything what the child needs, for example the good school and the nice house. Moreover, the women can build their career first, and after that they can come back to the work without losing their position.

However, this development also has the disadvantages. The first disadvantage is the medical one, because it is more difficult for the older women to become pregnant and there are more risks for the mother and the baby. Secondly, the older parents have less energy for playing with the small children, and they will be quite old when their child is a teenager. In addition, if everybody has the children later, the population of the country will decrease, and this is a problem for the economy in the future.

In conclusion, having the children at a later age has the advantages like the money and the maturity, but also the disadvantages like the health risks and the energy. Every family should decide by themselves what is the best for them.

question: In many countries, shopping is becoming a free time activity that replaces traditional hobbies, such as reading and sport. What are the reasons for this? Do you think this is a positive or negative development?
essay:
In several nations, shopping has become an increasingly popular leisure activity. A lot of people prefer it over conventional hobbies like reading or sports. The main reasons for this situation are the convenience and instant gratification it provides. I believe it is a negative development as it can have negative impacts on both individuals and society.

Indulging in shopping is a much easier and more gratifying experience. This is because it requires very little effort these days and can be done from anywhere, whether sitting at home, or in the workplace, whereas engaging in a sport may require a person to get ready and put in some physical work. This ease encourages individuals to spend more time buying things. Moreover, purchasing new things is simply more rewarding than reading, for example, as it releases dopamine in the brain , which is the primary hormone responsible for making people feel happy. For example, a young student would prefer to buy a new purse during her break time rather than reading additional pages of a novel , as a new purse will bring her joy almost immediately

However, no matter how appealing it seems, this situation can be more harmful than good. When young people shop more and more instead of doing productive activities like sports or reading, it makes them dull over time and can impact their holistic development. Also, such pastime will put additional strain on natural resources as more demand leads to more production. For example, the tendency of youngsters not to to repeat their outfits encourages them to hoard more clothes, which ultimately leads to over-utilization of available resources.

In conclusion, shopping is a preferred pastime over other traditional hobbies due to its ease and addictive reward system. Nevertheless, it can be highly detrimental for our future generation in terms of impacting their overall growth and draining their available stock of natural resources.

question: In some countries, cash is being replaced almost entirely by digital payment. Do you think this is a positive or a negative development?
essay:
In many countries nowadays, the people are not using the cash anymore and they are paying by the cards and the mobile phones. Some persons are saying this is a good change but some are not agree. I think this development is mostly positive because it is very convenient.

Moreover, all the transactions are recorded, so the government can catch the black money and the tax evasion is reducing.

Secondly, there are also some problems. The old people are not knowing how to use the smartphones and they are facing many difficulties in the shops. question: Increasingly, people pay a monthly subscription to use products such as software, cars, furniture and even clothing, instead of buying them outright. Do you think this is a positive or a negative development?
essay:
In these days, many companies are selling their products by subscription, for example the software, the cars and even the clothes. The customer pays every month and he can use the product, but he is not the owner. Some people think this is a good trend, but I think it is mostly a negative development.

Of course, there are some benefits of subscription. The first one is that people do not need to pay a big amount of money at one time. For example, a new car is very expensive, but if you pay monthly, even the young people can drive a new car. This is especially useful for the students and for people who have just started working. Also, the company will repair the product if it is broken, so the customer does not need to worry about it.

However, I believe the disadvantages are more important. Firstly, in the long term the customer pays much more money than buying. If a person uses a software for ten years, the total cost of the subscription will be very high. Secondly, many people forget about their subscriptions and they continue paying for the things which they are not using anymore. Companies know this and they make the cancellation very difficult. Thirdly, when the customer stop paying, he loses everything, and he have nothing at the end.

In conclusion, although subscription is convenient and it is easy to pay, I think it is a negative development because people pay more money and they do not own anything. People should think carefully before they choose the subscription.

question: Nowadays, most of the information is available on the Internet, whereas in the past, knowledge was stored in books and on paper. Do you think the advantages of this situation outweigh its disadvantages?
essay:
It is widely acknowledged that information requires great consideration when it comes to its availability and storage. While people find a significant amount of knowledge on the internet, in the past, there were books and papers where information can be stored.I strongly believe that the advantages of the internet, such as providing more affordable and efficient access to information, far outweigh its drawbacks, including the risk of spreading misinformation. This essay will elaborate on both sides and my position with relevant arguments and examples.

On the one hand, the internet is an accessible tool for anyone who wants to improve their knowledge about a topic, which books cannot accomplish. People can use search engines, such as Google, for free to find very specific details on the internet, allowing them to shorten their research time and look into other information sources. For instance, rather than purchasing expensive books and going to a library, students can connect to the internet from home and download PDFs of books they cannot afford to buy, for free, on Google Scholar. Therefore, the internet provides not only time-saving opportunities, but also budget-friendly options, which books cannot offer.

On the other hand, one of the main drawbacks of the internet in terms of information is that misinformation can swiftly spread through some unreliable sources. This is because there is no authority to check whether each piece of information is true or fake, which allows some users to edit and share fake news and misinformation. To illustrate, Wikipedia is a public information website where users can contribute to topics; however, some information becomes unreliable due to the lack of regulations. Thus, misinformation forces people to check other online sources to verify the reliability of the information, whereas books are already verified before being published.

In conclusion, although there are some disadvantages of the internet, I firmly maintain that online sources can provide many considerable opportunities for anyone. Since most of them are free to use and help people manage their research time, these advantages outweigh the drawbacks of misinformation.

question: Some people think that children should begin learning a foreign language at primary school rather than secondary school. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
essay:
There is no doubt that learning a foreign language has become increasingly important in today’s globalized world. While some people believe that children should start studying a foreign language in secondary school, others argue that primary school is a more suitable stage. In my opinion, the benefits of introducing foreign languages at an early age outweigh the drawbacks.

One of the main advantages of learning a foreign language in primary school is that young children can acquire languages more easily than older students. At an early age, children have a stronger ability to imitate pronunciation and remember vocabulary. As a result, they can develop better communication skills and become more confident in using another language. Furthermore, learning a foreign language helps improve cognitive abilities such as problem-solving and critical thinking.

Another benefit is that early language education can provide children with greater opportunities in the future. In today’s competitive job market, bilingual or multilingual individuals often have an advantage. Moreover, learning about another language also exposes children to different cultures, which can encourage tolerance and respect for diversity.

However, there are some disadvantages. Some people argue that primary school students should focus more on core subjects such as mathematics and science. Adding another subject to the curriculum may increase pressure on young learners. Nevertheless, these challenges can be minimized if schools use engaging and age-appropriate teaching methods.

In conclusion, although introducing foreign languages in primary school may create some additional pressure, the long-term benefits, including improved language skills, cognitive development, and better career prospects, make it a worthwhile approach.

question: Some people have decided to reduce the number of times they fly every year or to stop flying altogether. Do you think the environmental benefits of this development outweigh the disadvantages for individuals and businesses? essay:
There is no denying the fact that transportation means have an effect on environmental health. While it is a commonly held belief that reducing the number of flights is important for the ecosystem, there is also an argument that flying is crucial for people's lives. This essay will analyse this topic from both views and express my opinion.

On the one hand, some people believe that using air travel has a detrimental effect on our planet. This is because travelling to another city or country requires using fast means like a plane, which requires a large amount of fuel, which the engines burn to allow the plane to fly. These constant emissions pollute our atmosphere. For example, during the COVID-19 pandemic, the number of flights was reduced, and air pollution declined significantly.

On the other hand, some people claim that making a restriction on travelling by air is directing individuals to use another kind of transportation. In other words, people need to use their private vehicles or public buses to travel long distances. This also has a harmful effect on the environment. For instance, when every person drives his own car, this will produce a lot of gas emissions that cause an environmental crisis, especially for humans, because cars are driven on land.

In conclusion, there are no easy answers to this question. On balance, however, I believe that everything in life has pros and cons. We need to use them wisely, so we can enjoy them without being deprived of their benefits.

question: In some families, young children are cared for during the working day by their grandparents. Others believe that professional nurseries provide a better start. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

question: In some countries, people who are unemployed receive a sum of money each week in the form of a benefit, while some support this, other people believe that this money should not be given. Discuss both points of view and give your own point of view
essay:
There has always been a controversy regarding whether giving money in the form of a benefit each week to unemployed people is a good idea or not. Some people claim that this can help support families with financial issues. While others oppose  this idea, it can be expensive for the government. This essay will discuss both views, followed by my personal opinion.

On one side of the argument, people believe that the benefit can help citizens afford basic needs such as, food, rent, and bills. This financial support can prevent unemployed individuals and their families from falling into poverty. Although the amount of money may not be enough to cover all their expenses, it can still help them pay for necessities. Not only that, but these payments can also reduce crime, and people feel less pressured while looking for a new job. Not only that, but having this backing can also help families maintain a good relationship, as financial problems can sometimes create tension at home.

On the other hand, some people believe that unemployment benefits can make citizens too dependent on the government. For instance, if someone gets regular payment every week, they may become less motivated to find a job quickly. However, this problem can be controlled if the government only gives the money for a certain period of time and asks citizens to prove they are looking for a job.Another reason why people think unemployment benefits are a bad idea is because it can cost the nation a lot of money. The society feels as if the money could be used on schools or hospitals instead. For example, more funding for the schools could help build new classrooms , or if this money goes to hospitals, they can improve medical equipment.

In my opinion, I believe unemployment benefits should be given as they can help individuals pay for basic needs and reduce stress while they are looking for a new post. Although some may become dependent on this money, these problems can be reduced by giving  aid only for a limited time.  With this argument, I firmly conclude that the advantages are greater than the disadvantages.

question: Some people argue that it is useful to do research into family history. To search for past generations. However others believe that it is better to think more about the present and future generations. Discuss both view, give your opinion
essay:
Some people believe that researching past generations and learning about ancestors is vital, while others think it is more important to prioritise future generations and live in the present. I support the view that studying past generations and learning more about family history is valuable.

On the one hand, people’s desire to focus on future generations and live in the present is largely driven by the natural instinct to protect their families and leave the best possible conditions for future generations. In other words, this instinct developed thousands of years ago and still influences the way people think today. Many individuals prefer to focus on their children and descendants rather than spend considerable time learning about their ancestors. Although attitudes may vary across different cultures and geographical regions, the main logic behind focusing on future generations comes from the desire to leave a legacy and provide the best possible conditions for one’s children.

On the other hand, I agree with the perspective that it is crucial to deepen our knowledge of past generations. There is a famous saying that without knowing your past, you cannot build your future. This strongly resonates with the view I support, and I deeply believe that it is not only about studying history and reading old books; researching one’s family tree can eventually help people develop a stronger sense of identity and purpose. Without knowing where we come from or what our ancestors experienced and went through, it may be more difficult to build a better future for our children.

To sum up, although it is important to focus on the present and future, I believe it is equally, if not more, important to have knowledge of previous generations, and I maintain that researching our past can be highly valuable.

question: Some people believe that zoos are inhumane and should be closed down. Others argue that zoos play an important role in wildlife conservation. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay:
Opinions are divided on whether zoological parks should be permanently shut down due to ethical concerns or maintained for their ecological benefits. While confining animals to enclosures is often criticized as cruel, I am a huge advocate for modern zoos, provided they prioritize top-notch conservation and rehabilitation programs.

On the one hand, opponents of zoos argue that holding wild animals in captivity is inherently inhumane. Their primary concern is that artificial enclosures, regardless of how well-designed they are, can never fully replicate the vast natural habitats these creatures require for survival. Consequently, many confined animals suffer from severe physical and psychological distress, often exhibiting abnormal, repetitive behaviors known as zoochosis. For instance, large roaming predators like tigers and polar bears frequently struggle to adapt to limited spatial boundaries. This reality leads critics to assert that exploiting animals primarily for human entertainment is an outdated and deeply unethical practice that should be abolished.

On the other hand, supporters emphasize the prodigious impact that accredited zoological institutions have on global wildlife preservation. In an era where countless species face imminent extinction due to rampant deforestation and illegal poaching, modern zoos act as vital biological sanctuaries. They provide a safe haven for vulnerable creatures and fund extensive captive breeding programs designed to restore dwindling genetic pools. A prime example is the successful recovery of the Arabian Oryx, a species that was brought back from the brink of extinction through dedicated zoo breeding initiatives before being safely reintroduced into its natural habitat.

Overall, while the ethical arguments against depriving animals of their freedom are valid, the critical role of regulated zoos in safeguarding global biodiversity cannot be ignored. Therefore, rather than closing all facilities, authorities must ensure they transition strictly into dedicated research and conservation reserves where animal welfare supersedes commercial entertainment.

question: Some people believe the government should spend money on building train and subway lines to reduce traffic congestion. Others think that building more and wider roads is the better way to reduce traffic congestion. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay:
It is often argued that governments should spend money on building train and subway lines to reduce traffic congestion, while others believe that constructing more and wider roads is a better solution. Both perspectives have some valid points. However, I personally support the view that governments should prioritise public transport because it can carry large numbers of passengers and reduce dependence on private vehicles.

On the one hand, I support the idea that governments should invest more in train and subway systems. One key reason for this is that public transport can carry a large number of passengers at the same time. This is mainly because a single train can transport hundreds of people, whereas the same number of passengers would require many private cars. In other words, public transport uses road space more efficiently. For example, a subway can carry thousands of commuters during peak hours. As a result, fewer vehicles may be present on busy roads. Another important point is that efficient public transport can reduce dependence on private cars. This is because people are more likely to leave their cars at home when convenient alternatives are available. For instance, daily commuters may choose a subway instead of driving to work. Consequently, fewer private vehicles can lead to lower traffic congestion. Overall, I believe this perspective is more convincing.

On the other hand, some people argue that building more and wider roads is a better solution. The main reason for this position is that additional road space can improve traffic flow in congested areas. One explanation is that wider roads can increase capacity and allow vehicles to move more smoothly. For example, an additional lane may reduce bottlenecks on a major road. As a result, road expansion can provide immediate relief in certain locations. Therefore, it is understandable why some people support this view.

In conclusion, although wider roads have some valid benefits, I remain convinced that investment in trains and subway systems is the more convincing approach. This is mainly due to their ability to transport large numbers of passengers and reduce dependence on private vehicles.

question: Some people say government should give health care the first priorities, some others believe education is more important priorities to spend the taxpayers' money. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay:
It is often argued that governments should give healthcare the highest priority, while others believe that education is more important when spending taxpayers’ money. Both views have some valid arguments and can be supported for different reasons. However, I personally believe that healthcare should receive greater priority because it improves physical health and enhances people’s quality of life.

On the one hand, I believe that healthcare should receive greater priority. The primary reason for my view is that public investment in healthcare improves physical health. This is mainly because it provides affordable medical services and preventive care. In other words, people can receive timely treatment and avoid serious diseases. For example, free vaccinations and health screenings can help detect preventable diseases early. As a result, overall public health can improve. Furthermore, another important reason is that better healthcare enhances people’s quality of life. This is because accessible medical services help people remain healthy and active. For instance, proper treatment can help older people manage chronic diseases and live independently. Consequently, they can participate more actively in family and community life. Therefore, healthcare is the more beneficial approach.

On the other hand, some people believe that education should receive greater priority. The main reason for this view is that investment in education creates employment opportunities. This is mainly because educated people develop skills required by modern industries. For example, technical education can prepare young people for engineering and IT jobs. As a result, it can reduce unemployment. Therefore, it is understandable why some people support this view.

In conclusion, although there are valid arguments in favour of prioritising education, I personally believe that healthcare is the better option. This is mainly because it improves physical health and enhances quality of life.

question: Some people say History is one of the most important schoool subjects. Othert people think that, in todays world, subjects like Science and technolog are most important than History. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

question: Some people think advertisements may have positive economic effects whereas others think there are negative social effects because individuals are not satisfied with who they have. Discuss both views.
essay:
People have different views about advertisements. Some people think they are good for the economy. Others think they are bad for society, because they make people unhappy with what they have. In my opinion, the social problem is bigger, because ads change how people feel about their own lives.

People who support advertisements have one good reason: they help the economy. When a business shows an ad, more customers learn about its products. For example, a shoe company puts an ad on TV, and many people go to the shop to buy the new shoes. This means the company sells more, which gives it more money. Because of this, the company can hire more workers and open new shops. If many businesses do this, the country has more jobs and more money. So ads help the economy grow.

However, I believe that the social effect of ads is worse, because ads make people unhappy with what they have. For example, a teenager sees an ad with a new phone and a happy family. Then he looks at his old phone and thinks it is not good enough. He feels sad, so he asks his parents to buy a new one. Many families do not have enough money, so they feel stressed. Over time, people start to buy things they do not need, only to feel better. Because of this, they compare themselves with others, and they never feel happy with what they have. If this continues, society becomes less happy. This is why I think the bad social effect is bigger.

In conclusion, advertisements can help the economy, because companies sell more and give jobs to people. However, I believe that the social effect is worse, because ads make people feel that they need more. This is why ads can be a problem for society.

question: some people view the conflict between teenagers and parents as a necessary part of growing up, while others view it as something negative which should be avoided. discuss both views and give your own opinion. five reasons for your answer and include any relevant example from your knowloedge or experience.
essay:
It is often argued that disagreements between teenagers and their parents are a normal and necessary part of growing up. However, others believe that family conflict is harmful and should be avoided. In my opinion, some disagreement is useful because it helps teenagers become independent, but serious and continuous conflict should be prevented.

There are several reasons why conflict can be considered a natural part of adolescence. First, teenagers gradually develop their own opinions and want more independence. As a result, they may disagree with their parents about clothes, friends, schoolwork or the time they should come home. This can help them learn how to express their ideas and make their own decisions. Second, arguments can improve communication if both sides discuss their feelings calmly. For example, a teenager who explains why they want to choose a particular course may help their parents understand their goals. In this way, conflict can lead to greater trust and a more mature relationship.

On the other hand, frequent arguments can have negative effects. One problem is that constant conflict may cause stress and sadness for both teenagers and parents. Teenagers who feel that they are always criticised may lose confidence or become secretive. Another disadvantage is that serious conflict can damage family relationships. In extreme cases, young people may spend more time away from home or make risky decisions simply to show their independence. Therefore, although small disagreements are normal, aggressive shouting and personal insults should be avoided.

In my view, conflict is not completely negative. It is an important part of growing up because teenagers need to separate themselves from their parents and develop their own identity. Nevertheless, disagreements should be controlled through respectful conversation and clear rules. For instance, in many families, parents allow their children to choose their hobbies while still setting reasonable limits on study and bedtime. This can reduce unnecessary arguments.

In conclusion, conflict can teach teenagers independence and communication skills, but excessive conflict may cause stress and weaken family relationships. Therefore, healthy disagreement should be accepted, while destructive arguments should be avoided.

question: Technology has made it possible for people to work from home rather than commuting to an office. Some believe this is a positive development, while others argue it has significant disadvantages. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
In recent years, technology has allowed many people to do their job at home instead of going to their office every day. Some people think this is a positive development, but others believe there are many problems with it. In this essay, I will discuss both views and then give my opinion.

Firstly, working from home has many benefits for workers. People do not have to spend time and money on travelling to work, so they can save a lot of time. Moreover, many employees feel more comfortable when they work in their home environment, and they can be more productive. Parents with young children also benefit because they can spend more time with their family and they do not need to pay for childcare.

On the other hand, some people argue that working from home has many serious disadvantages. Firstly, workers who stay at home may feel lonely because they do not have contact with their colleagues every day. Communication between team members can also be very difficult when everyone works in a different place. In addition, some people find it is hard to concentrate at home because there are many distractions such as television and household tasks.

In my opinion, I think working from home can be a positive development if it is managed in a good way. Companies should use a hybrid approach where employees work some days at home and some days in the office. This will allow workers to enjoy the benefits of both environments. In conclusion, the best solution is a combination of home working and office working to ensure good communication and productivity.

question: Employers are now able to record everything their staff do on company computers. Some people believe that employers should be free to do this. Do you agree or disagree?
essay:
In the modern era, the technology is allowing the companies to see everything which the employees are doing on the office computers. Some people are saying that the employers should have the full freedom to do this monitoring. I do not fully agree with this, because the workers also have the right of privacy.

On the one hand, we can understand the employers. The computers and the internet connection are belonging to the company, and the company is paying the salary for the working hours. If some employees are wasting the time on the social media or on the shopping websites, the productivity is going down and the company is losing the money. Also, the monitoring can protect the important data, because sometimes the employees are stealing the information and selling it to the competitors.

On the other hand, too much monitoring is creating a bad atmosphere in the office. The employees are feeling that nobody is trusting them, and because of this the stress is increasing day by day. Moreover, sometimes people are using the office computer for the personal messages, for example to their family or to the doctor, and reading these messages is not fair for them. Everybody is needing some private space also, even in the office.

In conclusion, I think the employers can do some monitoring for the security reasons, but they should not read the personal messages of the employees, and they should tell the employees that the monitoring is happening. So the freedom should not be full.

question: Governments have limited budgets for health care. Some people believe that public money should always be spent on preventing illness rather than on treating it. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Nowadays, the health budget of the every country is limited and the government must decide how to use it. Some people believe that the money should be always used for the prevention of the diseases and not for the treatment. I agree with this idea to some extent, but I think the treatment is also very important.

Firstly, the prevention is cheaper than the treatment. If the government is spending the money on the awareness campaigns about the smoking, the junk food and the exercise, many people will not get the serious diseases like the diabetes and the heart problems. In this way, the government will save a lot of money in the future, because the treatment of these diseases is very expensive. Also the vaccination is a very good example, because one injection can save a person from the big illness.

Secondly, however, we can not forget the patients who are already sick. If all the money is going to the prevention, then who will treat these people? Every day the new patients are coming to the hospitals and they are needing the immediate help. The hospitals need the doctors, the machines and the medicines, and all these things are very costly. Their families are also depending on them. It is not humanitarian to leave the sick people without the treatment.

In conclusion, I agree that the prevention should get more money because it is cheaper and it is saving the future generations, but the government can not stop the treatment completely, so a good balance is necessary between the both.

question: Education should be free for everyone. To what extent do you agree?
essay:
Nowadays, it is argued that all students might pursue education without a tuition fee. While some disagree with this statement, I partly agree with it inasmuch as I truly believe that higher education should not be free for everyone. This essay will examine my point of view in detail.

To begin with, I’m convinced that states should fund schooling, just because it is compulsory. All democratic governments ideally provide free education, as their main goal for them is to supporting residents in acquiring basic knowledge and instilling social values. Such a policy has a positive effect on both the public and the country: if poor families cannot pay, educated citizens will maintain a stronger economy. To illustrate, I studied with an exceptionally clever and remarkably intelligent classmate from a low-income family at a state-funded school. He created a media platform when he was 15 with an IT teacher and then received a job offer from a sought-after Russian IT company. Thus, this example clearly illustrates my view that compulsory education should be free because all children from different families have the right to education.

However, there are exceptions in the case of higher education. I would argue that making it entirely free is unrealistic. Firstly, leading universities are extremely expensive to run, ranging from attracting highly qualified specialists to covering maintenance costs. If higher education were free for everyone, the state would have to either raise taxes significantly or compromise on quality. Secondly, not everyone wishes to pursue a degree: some people prefer to start working after school and gain practical experience instead. Therefore, funding higher education for all would be an inefficient use of public money. A more sensible approach would be a mixed system combining state funding, scholarships and student loans.

In conclusion, I partly agree that education should be free. While compulsory schooling must be funded by the state, making higher education entirely free is unrealistic. A mixed system, combining government funding, scholarships and student loans, would be the most effective solution.

question: environmental protection is the responsibility of politicians, not individuals as individuals can too little. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
In recent years, the topic of environmental protection has emerged as a significant concern for the general public. While some individuals contend that government takes responsibility for conserving the environment, I maintain that individuals play a vital role in addressing environmental issues. This essay will elucidate these differing perspectives.

On the one hand, it is essential to recognise that individuals should acknowledge the significant roles associated with authorities’ accountabilities. A crucial consideration is that governments are responsible for allocating money to environmental projects, which highlights that they can implement legislation to limit pollution, emissions and protect natural resources. For example, it is noteworthy that the state can invest in renewable energy, such as solar energy, wind or wave power in order to reduce reliance on fossil fuels. In addition, another important point to emphasise is that the authorities should improve the public transport systems. This is due to the fact that this encourages more people to use buses and trains, while the administration raises people’s awareness of preserving natural resources.

On the other hand, it is crucial to consider the opposing viewpoint that individuals have limited ability to solve environmental problems. A significant factor to explore is that many problems are too complex and widespread for individuals to tackle environmental issues on their own, which underscores that meaningful changes often require collective efforts. To illustrate this perspective, one might refer to environmental protection, where individuals can reduce their use of plastic, but this action alone is unlikely to solve the problem. Furthermore, it is essential to highlight that individuals often lack the resources to solve large-scale problems. This assertion is supported by the fact that governments have greater power to implement solutions that can affect millions of people.

In conclusion, although governments play a crucial role in protecting the environment by implementing legislation and investing in renewable energy, individuals shouldn’t be overlooked because their actions can contribute to environmental protection. Therefore, I believe that effective environmental protection requires shared responsibility and cooperation between governments and individuals.

question: Governments should invest more in public transport than in building new roads. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
The area on which the government spends its money is a highly controversial issue. Many people argue that the funds should be allocated towards public transport development, while others opine that it ought to be spent on building new roads. Personally, I strongly agree with the former statement.  The three reasons are that public transport can cut traffic, lower air harm and help people who cannot buy a car, making it justifiable to spend more on it rather than constructing new roads.

To begin with, the use of mass transit systems can reduce the recurring issue of traffic congestion, since fewer private cars will be on the road as more families opt for transportation modes such as buses. For this reason, individuals who travel daily can benefit from this, as it is less time-consuming for them to move from one place to another. To illustrate, in many Japanese cities such as Saitama, good train systems can reduce the need to drive, as the majority of the population uses the highly efficient public commuting network, which reduces their citizens' reliance on personal vehicles.  The roads are nearly empty while the trains are working in full swing.

Additionally, public transit services, particularly subways, are widely considered more environmentally friendly because the majority of them operate on electricity rather than petrol, effectively reducing greenhouse gas emissions, a major contributor to various health complications and global warming. Not only that, it moves people away from driving cars. As a result, burdens on the healthcare industry can be reduced as the incidence of pollution-related illnesses in a country declines.  Therefore, investments in public transport are advantageous , although money must also be spent on improving roads and creating new lines ,  more focus should be placed on the conveyance rather than roads.

Moreover, mass commuting networks are the most accessible form of transportation. For this reason, they are highly advantageous for individuals from low-income households, students, and the elderly, since some may not be able to afford cars or may not own any.

In conclusion, I completely agree with the assertion that the government should prioritise investing in the enhancement of public transit systems to ensure optimal traffic flow, environmental sustainability, and inclusivity for all members of society.

question: Governments should spend more money preventing common illnesses than treating people after they become sick. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is often argued that governments should spend more money preventing common illnesses than treating people after they become sick. However, I personally agree with this view because prevention can reduce the risk of health problems and reduce pressure on healthcare services.

The primary reason why I agree with this view is that preventing common illnesses can reduce the risk of health problems. This is mainly because healthy habits such as regular exercise and a balanced diet can help people avoid obesity and lifestyle-related diseases. In other words, prevention can stop some health problems before they become serious. For example, governments can encourage people to walk or cycle regularly and eat more fruits and vegetables through public-health programmes. As a result, people may become healthier and have a lower risk of common diseases. Therefore, governments should give greater priority to preventing illnesses.

Furthermore, another important reason why I agree with this view is that prevention can reduce pressure on healthcare services. This is because fewer people may require frequent medical treatment when common illnesses are prevented or controlled at an early stage. For instance, if a government successfully encourages citizens to maintain healthy lifestyles, hospitals may receive fewer patients suffering from obesity-related and other lifestyle diseases. Consequently, healthcare resources can be used more effectively for people who need necessary medical treatment. Therefore, I strongly agree with this view.

In conclusion, I firmly agree with the view that governments should spend more money preventing common illnesses than treating people after they become sick. This is mainly because prevention can reduce the risk of health problems and reduce pressure on healthcare services.

question: It is important for all towns and cities to have large public outdoor places like squares and parks. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?
essay:
Numerous large outdoor places for the public, such as squares and parks, are crucial to be built in all towns and districts. I absolutely agree with this idea, as it brings great benefits like reducing people's stress, increasing the town's economic development, and also providing positive impacts for the environment.

To begin with, public spaces can make people happy. This is because it can be a place for them to socialise with their friends, build good quality time with family, and create some fun moments. Therefore, this place can release their life burden. Furthermore, having squares and parks also grows the economic status, because many small enterprises would like to open a stand and sell their products there. For example, in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, there is one big square called Alun-Alun where many young adults spend their free time buying street food, like Takoyaki or Cilok, then sit down and have small talks with their relatives.

Not only those positive things, but large spaces, specifically parks, are good for the environment. A park is a green space where there are many trees planted. Therefore, the trees can supply more oxygen and process carbon dioxide that comes from pollution around the city. The bigger the park, the greater the positive impact.

In conclusion, I agree that all cities have to create large public spaces, since they bring numerous benefits. It can reduce society's life burden and develop the surrounding economy. Moreover, it is really good for the environment too.

question: Many manufactured food and drink contains high level of sugar, which causes many health problems. Sugary products should be made more expensive to encourage people to consume less sugar. Do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Many manufactured foods and drinks contain high levels of sugar, which can contribute to various health problems. Some people therefore believe that increasing the price of sugary products is an effective way to encourage people to consume less sugar. I disagree with this view because there are more effective ways to address excessive sugar consumption.

One reason why higher prices may not be an effective solution is that people often continue to buy sugary products despite price increases. Many processed foods and drinks are convenient and widely available, while some people may also develop strong preferences for sweet foods. Therefore, increasing their cost may not significantly change their eating habits. Instead, it could place an additional financial burden on households, particularly those with lower incomes, without addressing the underlying reasons for unhealthy diets.

A more effective approach would be to provide better education about healthy eating. Schools could teach children about the nutritional value of different foods and the health risks associated with excessive sugar consumption. This could help young people develop healthier eating habits from an early age, which may continue into adulthood. In addition, governments could introduce stricter regulations on food manufacturers by requiring them to reduce the amount of sugar in their products. This would make healthier choices more accessible to the general population without relying solely on consumers to change their behaviour.

In conclusion, I do not believe that making sugary products more expensive is the best way to reduce sugar consumption. Health education and government regulation of food manufacturers would be more effective long-term solutions.

question: Some people believe that voting in national elections should be compulsory for all adult citizens. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
In some countries the citizens must vote in the election and if they do not vote they pay a fine. Some people think that this system should be used in every country. I do not agree with this opinion completely, because the voting is a right and not a duty, but I understand the reason of this idea.

Firstly, the supporters of this idea say that when everybody votes, the government is more representative. It is true that in many countries only the half of the people go to vote, and most of them are old and rich. So the young people and the poor people do not have the voice, and the politicians do not care about them. If the voting is compulsory, the politicians must think about all the citizens.

However, in my opinion the freedom is more important. In a democracy, the people have the right to choose, and this right include also the right to not choose. If a person does not like any candidate, why he must vote? Moreover, if the people are forced, they will vote without thinking, only for finishing quickly, and this is not good for the democracy.

Also I think the real problem is not the law but the trust. Many people do not vote because they think all the politicians are the same and nothing will change.

In conclusion, I disagree that the voting must be compulsory, because it can not solve the real problem and it takes away the freedom of the citizens, although I agree that the low participation is a serious problem for the democracy.

question: Many people feel it is a waste of money to try to save endangered animal species ,for example the tiger or the blue whale . To what extend do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Many people think that spending money to protect endangered animals, such as tigers and blue whales, is a waste of money. I disagree with this opinion because these animals are important for nature, and protecting them can also help people.

Firstly, every animal has an important role in the environment. If one species disappears, it can affect other animals and plants. For example, tigers help control the number of other animals in forests. Without them, the balance of nature could be damaged. Therefore, governments should spend money on protecting endangered species.

Secondly, endangered animals can bring benefits to people. Many tourists travel to see rare animals in national parks, which helps local businesses and creates jobs. In addition, scientists study these animals to learn more about nature and sometimes make new discoveries that can help humans. Because of this, protecting wildlife is a good investment for the future.

Some people believe that money should only be spent on problems like healthcare, education, or poverty. These are very important issues, but governments can support both people and the environment. If we do not protect endangered animals today, future generations may never have the chance to see them.

In conclusion, I do not think it is a waste of money to save endangered species. They are important for the environment, they can help the economy, and they should be protected for future generations.

question: Schools and workplaces should allow people to make mistakes without serious consequences because failure is an important part of learning. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is often argued that schools and workplaces should allow people to make mistakes without serious consequences because failure is an important part of learning. However, I personally agree with this view because it can develop problem-solving and independent thinking and increase people's confidence and motivation.

The primary reason why I agree with this view is that allowing people to make mistakes can develop problem-solving and independent thinking. This is mainly because people can identify their mistakes and think about how to solve problems more effectively. In other words, mistakes can give people an opportunity to learn through their own experience instead of always depending on others. For example, a student who makes a mistake while completing a practical project can examine the problem and find a better way to complete the task. As a result, the student can improve problem-solving skills and become more independent. Therefore, I believe that people should be allowed to make reasonable mistakes during the learning process.

Furthermore, another important reason why I agree with this view is that a supportive environment can increase people's confidence and motivation. This is because encouragement and positive feedback can make people more willing to make an effort and improve their performance. For instance, a teacher may explain a student's mistake and encourage the student to try the task again instead of giving a severe punishment. Consequently, the student may become more confident and motivated to improve. Therefore, I strongly agree with this view.

In conclusion, I firmly agree with the view that schools and workplaces should allow people to make mistakes without serious consequences. This is mainly because it can develop problem-solving and independent thinking and increase people's confidence and motivation.

question: Should a city try to preserve its old, historic buildings or destroy them and replace them with modern buildings? Use specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
essay:
In the modern era, whether we should save the historical centres or build a modern development to replace them  is a topic of considerable debate. I strongly believe that preserving an old building can help us to increase economic growth and preserve the cultural identity of that place.

Firstly, old architecture represent the cultural value of that area. Also, it is a main cultural identity that tells a story of the past to that country. Because of its unique architectural design and traditions peoples want to save them for  future generations. In addition, historic landmarks are an indispensable asset of that country. For example, Rome has become the world's best tourist place to see the historical landmarks because of preserving the heritage structures from the last 100 years of that country.

Lastly, conserving the historic landmark can help them to increase economical growth of that country.

Therefore, so many places which has historicals places become a main attraction for tourists. Tourists often choose the destination which was built in the past . So, it's become a great source of money to increase the financial value of that area. Also, it's add the value to the peoples employement and job security by working in restaurants and hotels that are near  the attractions. For instance, the Taj Mahal is India's greatest tourist attraction. So, people who work as a tourist guide or in a hotel in the agra earn a good amount of salary. However, constructing new centres from old structure wants a lot of money and energy for resources, contributing to environmental waste.

In a nutshell, cities should prioritise the old architectural buildings because they contribute in economical growth and save the cultural identity of that place. New construction may demolish the value of that city's past.

question: The best way to understand other cultures is to work for a multinational organisation. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Some argue that the most effective way of understanding different cultures is by working for a multinational organisation. Although this can be a good approach, I believe that people choose to work in a particular place for other reasons, and that education and travelling are more effective ways of learning about different societies.

People generally choose to work for a particular organisation for reasons other than learning about different societies. Most individuals work to achieve their career goals, earn a good salary, and fulfil their professional ambitions rather than to learn about unrelated subjects. Therefore, learning about different traditions and ways of life is more likely to be an additional benefit than a priority for most employees. Moreover, co-workers may not always discuss their backgrounds, as they may not have a strong interest in learning about each other. For example, many fresh graduates in Saudi Arabia choose multinational organisations to build a strong CV and gain better career opportunities because of their good reputation.

Education and travelling can provide people with more opportunities to learn about other societies. Through books, documentaries, reliable sources, and guided tours, individuals can learn about the history, traditions, and lifestyles of different communities in greater depth. In contrast, employees may not have enough time to explore these aspects because of their work and personal responsibilities. Travellers, however, usually have more time and motivation to learn about the countries they visit. For example, streaming platforms such as Netflix and Amazon Prime offer documentaries about different traditions and lifestyles, allowing people to gain  insight into other societies from home. Therefore, I believe this approach is not enough on its own and learning from other sources and different activities is more effective.

In conclusion, although working for a multinational organisation can expose people to different backgrounds, I believe that travelling and educating oneself through books and documentaries are more effective ways of understanding them. This is because people generally work to achieve professional goals, whereas travelling and education allow individuals to dedicate more time to learning about other societies.

essay:
The belief that humans have more power than other living organisms has been passed on through many generations over centuries. This is embedded in our attitude that we can deforest, expand our living area and hunt wild animals for pleasure without considering the consequences. One of the main effects is a decline in the number of animal species. This passage aims to discuss the causes and the suggested solutions for this problem.

A drastic growth of the human population leads to a huge demand for space to live, do agriculture and work, leading to  deforestation for urban development. It causes the reduction of the area for animals' habitat. question: Despite the large number of gyms, a sedenatary lifestyle is gaining popularity in the contemporary world. What problems are associated with this? What solutions can you suggest?
essay:
The number of gyms has grown significantly over the years. However, gym membership has not increased at the same rate, and many people now lead largely sedentary lives. This trend brings serious consequences that need to be addressed.

The most serious problem is the rise in obesity, as people who spend most of their day sitting burn far fewer calories. This can lead to diabetes and other long-term conditions such as heart disease. Diabetes can make someone's life much harder whether they might lose a foot or leg if they do not start their treatment early. Moreover, sitting or lying in a bed all day might cause some can also harm mental health. Mentally, they can develop depression, lonelinessand anxiety. Exercise naturally improves mood, so people who rarely move lose one of the simplest ways of managing stress.

Several practical measures could encourage people to become more active. Since many people sit at desks all day, employers could provide standing desks and encourage short walking breaks. Governments could build safer cycling routes and pedestrian-friendly streets, making it easier to walk instead of drive. Schools could increase physical education lessons, helping children build active habits early. Taxing short car and taxi journeys could also encourage walking. For example, someone who has just left a train station and needs a grocery store ten minutes away would walk rather than pay the extra cost of a taxi.

In conclusion, a sedentary lifestyle contributes to both physical conditions such as obesity and mental problems such as depression. Encouraging movement at work, school, and in city design could help reverse this trend.

question: Family members and friends caring for elderly people find it hard to spend enough time looking after them. What are the causes of this problem? What solutions can you suggest?
essay:
Nowadays, it is seen that youngsters do not have sufficient time to spend with their aged parents and to take care of them. There are many reasons, and there are also some solutions for this. Both the causes and solutions are discussed further in the ensuing paragraphs.

The foremost reason for this problem is the busy work schedule of the individuals. Nowadays , due to the high rate of expense people have to do a double job. There are many people who are not able to fulfil the basic needs of family members with only one job. To add to this, both husband and wife work. So they also do not get enough time to spend with each other. Sometimes it happens that due to a busy schedule, they feel tired. All these things become a huddle for them to spend time with the elderly.

One of the solutions for this problem is that the work can be divided between both husband and the wife. The work should be done by both of them. It should not be something only wives have to do, or only husbands have to do. Also, there can be a rule in the house that once a day, everyone sits together for a meal. They can spend holidays with family members. For example, on the day of Sunday, they can go for an outing. They can all play indoor games with each other.

To sum up, it can be said that every problem has a solution. So if , due to busy work conditions, they cannot spend time with each other, there are many alternatives for the same. So one just needs positive thinking to find some time for aged people.

question: In many wealthy countries, a large proportion of the food that is produced is never eaten and ends up being thrown away. What problems does this cause? What measures could be taken to reduce the amount of food that is wasted?
essay:
Nowadays, in many rich countries, a lot of food is thrown away every day by the families, the restaurants and the supermarkets. This is a big problem for the environment and also for the society. In this essay I will discuss the problems of food waste and some solutions to reduce it.

The first problem is that the food waste is harmful for the environment. When the food goes to the landfill, it produces bad gases which cause the global warming. Also, a lot of water and energy is used to grow the food and transport it, so when we throw it away, all these resources are wasted too. Another problem is that it is not fair. There are many poor people in the world who do not have enough food to eat, but in rich countries people throw the good food in the bin every day. Moreover, the families waste their money when they buy food and it go bad in the fridge.

There are some solutions which can reduce this problem. Firstly, people should plan their shopping and buy only the things they really need. They can make a list before they go to the supermarket. Secondly, supermarkets should give their extra food to the charities instead of throwing it, so the poor people can eat it. Thirdly, the government should build more recycling centres where the food waste can be change into the fertiliser or the energy.

In conclusion, food waste causes the environmental problems and it is also unfair for the poor people. I believe that if the people, the supermarkets and the government take these actions, the amount of wasted food will decrease significantly.
