For instance, it is widely known that kids need to be thoroughly watched by their teachers to be sure that they take their classwork seriously and do not fool around when classes are going on. Sadly, this is a task robotic teachers will be incapable of carrying out. Therefore, this makes it clear that classroom teachers will never be totally substituted by mechanisation.

Secondly, the learning process of students would be disrupted if they are taught by robotic teachers, which may slow down some students’ ability to comprehend information taught in lessons. For example, kids love to be motivated before lessons are taught effectively. This is a quality that many human teachers have , but robotic teachers do not have. Thus, it becomes apparent that human teachers will never be replaced by robotic teachers in a classroom.

To summarise, a robotic teacher does not have the necessary discipline to properly give instructions to students and actually works to retard the ability of a student to comprehend new lessons. Therefore, it is clear that the idea of running a classroom completely by a machine cannot be supported. After thorough analysis of this subject, it is predicted that the adverse effects of the debate over technology-driven teaching will always be greater than the positive effects, and because of this, classroom teachers will never be substituted for technology.

question: University students always focus on one specialist subject, but some people think universities should encourage their students to study a range of subjects in addition to their own subject. To what extent do you agree
essay:
In recent years, it has been observed that there are different views regarding focusing on specific subjects. Some people argue that students should study subjects outside their majors, while others believe that this wastes their time. I completely disagree with the view that university students should focus only on one specialist subject. This essay will examine the key reasons supporting this perspective, particularly developing different skills and discovering future career opportunities.

One main reason for this view is that studying different subjects allows students to develop a wider range of skills. In fact, these experiences make students more creative when they want to develop a new project. Not only does this help students become more inventive, but it also helps them solve problems in life. A study published by New York University concluded that students who followed this approach enhanced their knowledge.

Another fundamental reason is that studying different subjects can help students discover more career opportunities. This means that students are not limited to jobs related to their main major, and they can discover other fields that may suit them. A prime example is medical students who learn advanced AI skills. They can use their knowledge of both medicine and AI to find opportunities in technology companies. Consequently, this gives students more freedom to choose a career that suits their interests.

In conclusion, I strongly believe that universities should motivate students to study various subjects. This is mainly due to acquiring new skills and having more career choices. Overall, these factors support this perspective.

question: You have stayed at a friend’s house last weekend. You think you have left your watch there. Thank your friend describe your watch tell me what you want him to do write 150 words.
essay:
Dear Alex,

Thank you very much for inviting me over to your house in Toronto last weekend. It was a wonderful time celebrating your promotion at work and catching up with you and your family.

While it was a sombre time for us all, I will have to bother you with a request. I forgot my personal watch over there. I removed it before bed , and I left it on the dark brown table to the right of the bed. The table was near the window. It will be a stainless steel watch by Tissot with a green border design. If it is not there, then you can also check the coffee table in the hall.

If you find it, can you please mail it to my address at 45 Silverstone Drive in Etobicoke? My postal code is 1M6 3E5. If you cannot post it, then I can drop by to pick it up as well. If that is more feasible for you, then let me know what time works best for you this week.

Again, congratulations on your new role at work and my utmost apologies for this inconvenience. I look forward to your reply, Alex!

Best wishes,

Aditya

question: Many children today are overweight. This is a serious health problem Give the reasons responsible for child obesity and offer solutions to solve this problem.
essay:
Society has undergone massive changes, and one of these is the eating habits of young people.   Many children today suffer from being overweight.  This is a  very serious health concern. This essay will examine the reasons for child obesity and possible solutions to  address this issue.

On the one hand, there are multiple reasons responsible for child obesity.  First, a poor diet is a huge problem. While dining on fast food, children consume unbelievable amounts of carbohydrates and unhealthy fats.   Moreover,  processed foods constitute a large part of their diet.  Second, love of technology has resulted in a huge decrease in physical activity.  A recent study reported that children today spend about seven hours per day online, creating a sedentary lifestyle.  For example, children are not active as they sit in their rooms gaming or on social media.  Finally, a lack of knowledge and information is a problem.  Parents, and their children, lack health literacy.  They lack the proper facts about diet, calories, and child wellness.  

On the other hand, there is a wide range of solutions to deal with this problem.  First and foremost is to change and improve the dietary habits.  Eliminating foods that are high in calories and carbohydrates would be a good start.  Also, unhealthy processed snacks should be replaced by fruits and vegetables. Next,  children should be encouraged  to participate in  exercise and organised sports. They could join clubs and engage in daily workouts.  Also, parents should limit the hours spent on the computer. Finally, there needs to be an awakening.  Schools need to teach health and wellness courses, informing students of the facts. Also, parents must learn to read labels and be smarter grocery shoppers.

In conclusion, it is abundantly clear that childhood obesity is driven by several factors.  However,there are  many solutions available to address this problem

question: Many people spend too much time using social media. What problems can this cause, and what solutions can you suggest?
essay:
Nowadays, many people spend too much time using social media. I believe that it causes a lot of problems, such as eye infections and psychological diseases.  This is because it takes us away from reality. Therefore, I can suggest several solutions, including monitoring and setting limits.

On the one hand, spending too much time on social media can cause various eye problems, including eye infections and irritation. This is because screen emissions affect the eyes with long-term use. For example, in 2025, I went to an ophthalmologist because my eyes were red and itchy, and he advised me to wear blue-light-blocking glasses and not use social media for more than half an hour at a time. Therefore, I suggest an arrangement not to use social media more than three times a week, with an alarm set every half hour.

On the other hand, long use of social media is linked to some psychological diseases, including depression and Autism. In other words, they happen because of a loss of communication skills and poor analytical ability. For instance, one of my relatives spends a lot of time on social media, and his ability to express himself correctly has declined; in addition, he likes to stay alone. As a result, it creates a big gap in people's abilities. My suggestion is to get together with others to minimise the risks, especially by monitoring each other.

In conclusion, both sides present the causes and suggestions for too much social media use to address this important issue. Therefore, I believe we must be more organised and manage our social media use.

question: Obesity is becoming a growing concern in many developed countries. What are the main causes of obesity, and what solutions can be taken to tackle this issue?
essay:
In recent years, obesity has become a major health crisis in many developed countries. It is mainly caused by unhealthy dietary habits  and a sedentary lifestyle. This issue can be addressed through government interventions and large-scale health education campaigns.

One of the main causes of obesity is a lack of physical activity. In developed countries, generally, most people have comfortable lifestyles and sedentary jobs, so they engage in less physical activity and burn fewer calories. As a result, excessive calorie consumption can lead to weight gain and increase the risk of obesity-related diseases.  Additionally, the widespread availability of fast food and sugary snacks encourages people to consume excessive calories beyond the body’s daily requirements, eventually leading to more unhealthy weight gain.

To combat obesity, governments should implement several effective interventions. First and foremost, governments should introduce large-scale health education programs to raise public awareness about healthy lifestyles and health problems associated with obesity through television and ,most importantly , social media platforms such as Facebook and TikTok. Another effective solution would be increasing  taxes on calorie-dense food and limiting access to highly processed food. This can help people to resist the temptation to consume fast food.Additionally, local authorities should build more green spaces and sports centers where the public can engage in outdoor activities and some sports as maintaining a healthy lifestyle and engaging in regular physical activity go hand in hand.

All in all, although modern lifestyle and easy access to fast food can inevitably lead to obesity, it can be successfully tackled by raising public awareness about  obesity and increasing taxes on unhealthy food products.

question: We are becoming increasingly dependent on computers. They are used in business, hospitals, crime detection and even to fly planes. What things will they be used for in the future? Is this dependence on computers a good thing or should we be more suspicious of their benefits?
essay:
In the last two decades cybernetics have experienced a major breakthrough .This led to the utilization of computers in nearly all parts of our daily life, from personal computers to the ones performing complicated surgeries. Surely the uptake of this technology facilitates a lot of difficult tasks but is this excessive dependance ripping the warmth out of our lives? In this essay, I will outline how the availability of computers affects our lives .

Most of the daily tasks an individual experiences are time and effort consuming. These two fundemental qualities could be tremendously saved by the use of computers. The average period required to prepare a decent meal for a middle-class family is around an hour to and hour and a half when using traditional methods. This time could be literally reduced to half if computerized decives are used instead. Moreover, a busy businessman is enabled to easily close a profitable deal with just a touch on this highly programmed laptop while enjoying his family vacation and not having to exert an extra effort of traveling long distances in order to sign a deal.

On the other hand, new generations are growing remarkably dependent on these modern utilities, which makes them handicapped when it comes to preparing a cup of tea. Inaddition , psychologists suggest that one of the main reasons for sucidal rate increase is the recent electric inventions. This is due to the fact that humans by nature stay emotionally healthy through socializing, but due to the importance of modern technology to maintain a financially satisfying standard of life they gradually isulate themselves. As time passes by each of these individuals gets stuck in a vicious circle of loneliness that eventually leads to suicidal attempts especially among youngsters.

In conclusion, similarly to every other invention computers have their benefits and drawbacks, I personally think it all depends upon how we use the given tools . Moderation is the key here to keep the balance and allow us to live in harmony.

question: Some people think money is one of the most essential factors in promoting hapinness. Do you think people can be happy without much money? What other factors contribute towards happiness?
essay:
Some people believe that money is one of the most important factors in achieving happiness. While having sufficient money can certainly make life more comfortable, I believe that people can be happy without being wealthy. In fact, relationships, good health and a sense of purpose can contribute significantly to a person’s happiness.

To begin with, money is important because it provides people with financial security and allows them to afford basic necessities. Having enough income to pay for food, housing, healthcare and education can reduce stress and provide a sense of stability. Moreover, money gives people opportunities to enjoy leisure activities, travel and pursue their interests. However, once people have enough money to meet their essential needs, earning more does not necessarily make them happier. For example, a person with a modest income may lead a satisfying life if they have a supportive family and a strong social circle.

There are several other factors that can have a greater influence on happiness. First and foremost, meaningful relationships are essential because people generally need emotional support and companionship. Spending quality time with family members and close friends can create a sense of belonging that money cannot easily provide. Good physical and mental health is another important factor. A person who is healthy is more likely to enjoy everyday activities and maintain a positive outlook on life. Furthermore, having a sense of purpose, such as a fulfilling career, personal goals or helping others, can give people satisfaction and make their lives more meaningful.

In conclusion, although money is necessary for meeting basic needs and achieving financial security, it is not the only source of happiness. Strong relationships, good health and a meaningful purpose in life can be equally, or even more, important. Therefore, people can certainly live happy and fulfilling lives without having a great deal of money.

question: Around the world, people are now living longer than ever before in the past. Some say an ageing population creates problems for goverments. Others believe there are benefits to society having more elderly people. To what extent do the advantages of possessing an ageing population outweigh the disadvantages?
essay:
There is no denying the fact that people are living longer than in the past, and this has led to an increase in the number of elderly communities in many countries. While ageing dwellers can create some problems for governments, as well as several benefits. In my opinion, the advantages slightly outweigh the disadvantages.

To begin with, there are many disadvantages of having an ageing culture. Firstly, governments may need to spend more money on healthcare and pensions for the elderly community. In other words, the older generation usually needs more medical treatment and financial support after they stop working. In addition, a large elderly population can reduce the number of people in the workforce. For example, if many workers retire at the same time, there may be fewer youngsters available to work and pay taxes.

On the other hand, there are some important benefits of having a more elderly community in society. Firstly, the older crowd have a lot of experience and knowledge that can be useful to younger generations. It is also possible to say that they can help their families by taking care of children and giving advice. Moreover, many elderly people remain active and continue working or volunteering after retirement. For instance, retired teachers can help young students, while experienced workers can teach useful skills to younger employees.

In conclusion, there are both advantages and disadvantages to an ageing population. Although it can put pressure on healthcare systems, pensions and the workforce, I believe that the benefits are slightly greater because elderly people can provide valuable experience, support their families and contribute to society.

question: In many companies, software and artificial intelligence now carry out routine administrative work that was previously done by employees. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
essay:
Routine clerical work — invoicing, scheduling, first-line customer queries — is increasingly handled by software rather than staff. On balance I believe the advantages outweigh the disadvantages, provided that the workers affected are given genuine support.

The principal benefit is that organisations stop paying skilled people to do unskilled things. An administrator who spends three days a week copying figures between systems is not producing anything that could not be produced automatically, and the hours released can be redirected towards work that does require judgement, such as handling the complaints that software cannot resolve. Accuracy improves as well, since a system that has been correctly configured will not become careless at the end of a long afternoon. Most of the value, in other words, comes from removing work that nobody chose to do.

The obvious cost is employment. Administrative roles have historically offered stable, reasonably paid work to people without university qualifications, and there is no guarantee that the jobs created by automation will be accessible for the same group. Retraining is often proposed as the answer, but it is expensive and it assumes a willingness to start again in middle age that not everyone has. There is also a quieter risk: when a process is fully automated, the institutional understanding of how it works can disappear with the staff who used to run it.

Weighed against each other, I still consider the gains greater. The efficiency benefits are permanent and they compound, whereas the disruption, though severe, is concentrated in a transition that governments and employers can plan for. What matters is that the burden is not left entirely with the individuals who happen to be holding the affected jobs.

question: In many towns and cities, online retailers have taken a large share of the trade that once went to shops on the high street. Do the advantages of this shift outweigh the disadvantages?
essay:
Online retailers now take a substantial share of spending that previously went to town-centre shops, and the visible consequence is empty units on high streets. I think the advantages outweigh the disadvantages for most shoppers, though not for everyone and not for every town.

The gains to consumers are straightforward. Prices are lower because online sellers avoid the rent and staffing costs of a physical shop, and comparison is instant rather than a matter of walking between three stores. Range is the more significant advantage: a specialist item that no local shop could justify stocking is now routinely available, which matters most to people who do not live in a large city. Delivery also removes a barrier for anyone whose mobility, working hours or caring responsibilities made a shopping trip difficult.

The costs are concentrated rather than shared. Retail employed large numbers of people without formal qualifications, often locally and flexibly, and warehouse and delivery work has not replaced it on equivalent terms. The tax position compounds this, since a business rate levied on floor space falls entirely on the seller who has some. Town centres built around shops become unpleasant when the shops go, and an unpleasant town centre attracts less of everything else. There is a further group that loses outright: people who are not online, or who cannot receive deliveries, find their remaining options shrinking.

Weighing the two sides, the advantages still seem to me larger, because they are enjoyed by almost everyone while the disadvantages fall on smaller groups. But that is an argument for compensating those groups, not for pretending the losses are not real. Town centres that have found other uses for their space are doing considerably better than those still waiting for retail to return.

question: It is now common for people to change careers several times during their working lives. Why is this happening? Do you think it is a positive or a negative development?
essay:
A working life spent in a single occupation, once the norm, is now unusual in most developed economies. The shift has both an external cause and an internal one, and although it imposes real costs on individuals, I regard it overall as a positive development.

The external cause is that occupations themselves are less stable than they were. Automation and offshoring have removed whole categories of clerical, manufacturing and administrative work within a single generation, and the industries replacing them require different skills rather than the same skills applied elsewhere. Somebody whose trade disappears at forty does not choose to retrain; the alternative is unemployment.

The internal cause is a change in what people expect from work. Where a previous generation valued security above almost everything, many workers now treat a job as something that ought to develop them, and they are far more willing to leave when it stops doing so. The growth of flexible online study has made acting on that impulse realistic, since a qualification can be acquired alongside existing employment rather than instead of it.

The costs are obvious enough. Changing field usually means a drop in earnings and in seniority, and the permanent possibility of change is a source of anxiety, particularly for those with dependants or mortgages. But the alternative was never security for everyone; it was security for those whose industry happened to survive. A workforce that expects to retrain absorbs technological change far better than one built around jobs for life, and individuals who can move are less trapped by a single employer than those who cannot.

On balance, then, the development is positive, provided that governments treat retraining as a normal stage of a career rather than as emergency relief for the unlucky.

question: Many people now decide where to go on holiday because of photographs and videos they have seen on social media. Do you think this is a positive or a negative development?
essay:
Travel decisions that were once shaped by guidebooks and the recommendations of friends are now often made after a few seconds spent scrolling past other people's holiday photographs. Although this has made information about destinations far more accessible, I believe the overall effect is negative, largely because of what it does to the places being photographed.

The benefits should not be dismissed. Social media shows ordinary travellers what a place actually looks like, rather than only what a tourist board chooses to publish, and it has drawn attention to towns and landscapes that traditional guidebooks ignored. For a small guesthouse or a family restaurant with no advertising budget, a single widely shared video can bring more customers than years of conventional marketing.

The problem is that online attention is extremely concentrated. Platforms reward images that are already popular, so visitors do not spread out across a region; they converge on the same viewpoint, the same bridge and the same painted wall, often at the hour of the day when the light is best. Places that were never designed for large numbers of people, such as mountain paths or narrow village streets, are suddenly expected to absorb them, and residents bear the cost in noise, litter and congestion without sharing much of the income. The visitors lose something too, since a trip planned around recreating a particular photograph leaves little room for anything unplanned.

It is true that careful travellers can use these platforms for finding quieter alternatives. However, most people simply follow the most popular posts rather than looking beyond them, which is why I consider this development more harmful than helpful. Its advantages are real but thinly spread, whereas its disadvantages fall heavily on a small number of communities.

question: Many aspects of the way people dress today are influenced by global fashion trends. How has global fashion become such a strong influence on people's lives? Do you think this is a positive or negative development?
essay:
Global fashion has become an increasingly powerful influence on the way people dress, largely because of the rapid development of digital technology and social media. People across different countries are now exposed to the same styles, celebrities and online personalities, making fashion trends spread more quickly than ever before. In my opinion, this is largely a negative development because it can reduce individuality and encourage people, particularly younger generations, to seek social approval through their appearance.

One major reason global fashion has become so influential is the widespread use of social media platforms. People spend considerable amounts of time scrolling through applications such as TikTok and Instagram, where they are constantly exposed to international trends and influencer culture. In addition, algorithms repeatedly recommend content based on users’ previous interests, which means that similar styles are shown to them again and again. As a result, fashion trends can spread rapidly across national boundaries and become familiar to large numbers of people within a short period of time.

Another important factor is the human desire to fit in socially. Teenagers and young adults are especially vulnerable to peer pressure and are often influenced by what is considered fashionable within their social groups. For example, young people may follow viral clothing trends simply because they want to feel accepted by their peers. Consequently, they may begin to imitate the styles they see online without considering whether these trends genuinely reflect their personal tastes or identities.

I believe this development is negative because excessive conformity can gradually weaken individuality. When people repeatedly follow the same global trends, they may become less willing to experiment with their own style or express their personalities through clothing. Over time, this can result in greater similarity in the way people present themselves and may reduce the diversity that fashion traditionally allows. If individuals increasingly prioritise online approval over genuine self-expression, originality may become less valued.

In conclusion, global fashion has become highly influential because social media and digital technology allow trends to spread rapidly and encourage people to imitate widely accepted styles. Although global fashion can make international trends more accessible, I regard its overall impact as negative because it may undermine individuality and genuine self-expression.

question: Streaming platforms have largely replaced scheduled television and, for many people, trips to the cinema. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this change.
essay:
Watching at a time of one's own choosing has replaced watching at a time chosen by a broadcaster, and cinema attendance has fallen accordingly. The change has clear benefits for viewers, but its effects on what actually gets made are less comfortable.

The advantages for the audience are substantial and easy to state. Control over timing is the obvious one, and it matters most to the people whose hours are least predictable — shift workers, parents of small children, anyone for whom a fixed nine o'clock broadcast was simply unavailable. Beyond convenience, the range of material has widened enormously: series in other languages now reach audiences that a national broadcaster would never have commissioned them for, and older work that would once have vanished remains permanently available. Price is a further advantage for households that watch a great deal, though the proliferation of competing services has eroded it.

The disadvantages are less visible because they operate on production rather than on viewing. Platforms commission according to what their data suggests will retain subscribers, which favours material that resembles material that has already worked. The economics of cinema are affected too: a film that needs a large screen and a long run to find its audience is harder to finance when the default destination is a living room. Something is also lost socially — a broadcast watched by millions at once created a shared reference that a personalised library does not.

Overall the gains to viewers are real, and I would not want the schedule back. But it is worth being clear that convenience has been paid for in a currency the viewer never sees: a narrower range of things commissioned, and fewer occasions on which a whole country watches the same thing.

question: Nowadays, young people communicate with friends and family through mostly social network sites, rather than other ways of communication like talking on the phone or face to face. Do you think it is a positive or negative development
essay:
In recent decades, the public has been exposed to technology-driven resources, particularly social networks. Therefore, a significant number of young people prefer social networking platforms for chatting over face-to-face communication or talking on the phone. Regardless of the positive aspects, I firmly believe it is a predominantly negative development because online chats do not convey individuals’ feelings and social sites raise doubts regarding safety.

Emailing is a convenient way to share information quickly and also serves as a catalyst for communication cohesion. However, no online platform can replace a face-to-face conversation or hearing a familiar voice, as feelings and emotions are not transferable through a screen. For instance, a student may get a low score on an exam and need support, but an email cannot provide the comfort and reassurance that a face-to-face conversation can. Thus, this example alone expresses my view on the inability to share feelings through social networking platforms.

Debates about safety on the Internet are increasing, and nobody can prove that online chats can guarantee the protection of personal data. When people communicate through social networks, they often share private information, such as their location, photos, and personal opinions. This information can be misused by hackers, advertisers, or even criminals. For example, identity theft and cyberbullying are becoming more common, especially among young users who may not fully understand the risks. Unlike a private conversation in person, online chats leave a permanent digital footprint that can be accessed or leaked. Therefore, the lack of security is a serious drawback that cannot be ignored.

In conclusion, although social networking platforms offer convenience and speed, they cannot replace the emotional depth and safety of face-to-face communication. The inability to convey true feelings and the rising concerns about online safety make this trend predominantly negative. While technology will continue to evolve, it is essential to find a balance and not let digital chats completely replace real human interaction.

question: Some people think that good health is a basic human need and the medical service should not be run by profit-making companies. Do disadvantages outweigh advantages? Give your opinion.
essay:
Access to adequate healthcare is widely regarded as a fundamental human right, leading many to argue that medical services ought to be managed by public authorities rather than commercial enterprises. While allowing profit-making companies to operate in the healthcare sector does present certain economic advantages, I believe that the drawbacks—specifically regarding equity and quality of care—far outweigh the benefits.

On the one hand, private healthcare providers can introduce significant advantages through efficiency and innovation. Driven by the profit motive, private medical companies often invest heavily in state-of-the-art technology, advanced research, and modern infrastructure. This competitive drive can shorten waiting lists and attract top-tier medical professionals, offering a higher standard of comfort and specialized care for those who can afford it. Furthermore, private sector involvement can relieve some of the financial burden on state-funded healthcare systems by accommodating patients who would otherwise rely entirely on public hospitals.

On the other hand, the disadvantages of running medical services for profit are profound, primarily concerning social inequality. When healthcare is treated as a commodity, access is determined by financial capability rather than medical need. Consequently, lower-income populations may be priced out of essential treatments, preventive care, and life-saving medications, exacerbating societal divisions. Additionally, profit-driven management often prioritizes lucrative medical procedures over less profitable fields, such as mental health care or rural medicine, leaving critical public health needs unmet.

In conclusion, although the private sector brings financial investment and technological advancement to medicine, these benefits are overshadowed by the severe inequalities it creates. Because health is a universal necessity, I firmly believe that medical services should remain primarily under public stewardship to ensure equal access for all members of society, regardless of wealth.

question: some people think that hosting an international sporting event is beneficial for a country while others disagree. Do the advantages of hosting major sporting events outweigh the disadvantages?
essay:
Hosting major international sporting events, such as the Olympic Games or the Football World Cup, can bring both benefits and challenges to the host country. Although organising such events requires substantial investment and can cause temporary disruption, I believe the advantages outweigh the disadvantages because they can create employment and stimulate economic growth.

One major advantage of hosting an international sporting event is the positive impact it can have on the local economy. Such events attract thousands of domestic and international visitors who spend money on accommodation, food, transportation and entertainment. This increased demand allows local businesses to generate greater profits and may encourage them to recruit additional workers. As a result, more employment opportunities become available to local residents, enabling them to earn a stable income. Furthermore, increased consumer spending can generate additional tax revenue for the government, which can be invested in public services and infrastructure. Therefore, major sporting events can contribute considerably to the economic development of the host country.

Nevertheless, there are some significant disadvantages associated with hosting these events. A sudden influx of visitors can put considerable pressure on transportation systems, resulting in traffic congestion and longer commuting times for residents. Moreover, governments often have to spend substantial amounts of public money on stadiums, security and transport infrastructure. This may temporarily reduce the funding available for essential services such as healthcare and education. However, many of these problems are relatively short-term, while improved infrastructure and increased tourism can continue to benefit the country after the event has ended.

In conclusion, although hosting major sporting events can cause traffic problems and require significant initial investment, I believe the economic benefits are more substantial. Increased tourism, employment and business activity, together with improved infrastructure, can provide lasting benefits to the host country.

question: The topic of renewable energy is widely discussed these days. What are the main reasons behind the increasing use of renewable energy sources, and is this trend a positive or negative development for the environment?
essay:
In recent decades, the public and authorities have expressed concern about the ecological environment; consequently, green energy has become  a widely discussed topic. Using renewable energy tends to be a growing trend, inasmuch as the shortage of fossil fuels is a looming issue, and it is a cheaper way to generate electricity. I firmly believe that the increasing use of renewable energy sources is a positive development owing to its beneficial effects on the environment.

One of the principal reasons for widely implementing the renewable energy stations is that fossil fuel is the finite resources. Unlike coal, oil, and gas, natural sources will never run out, and humanities are guaranteed to avoid energy scarcity. Another justification for introducing is that solar panels and wind turbines require less expense for maintaining and producing energy than oil rigs and pipelines. To illustrate, wind and sun are free, and just construction and refurbishment require the investments.

Moreover, supporting green energy sources mitigates pollution issues. Transferring to such power reduces the carbon footprint and helps preserve natural ecosystems for future generations. Meanwhile, it reduces the negative impact of climate change. As a result, residents’ health tends to be improved by lowering air pollution-related diseases. For example, green stations are widely used in some regions in the USA, while urban communities are highlighting the improvement of the air quality there, and doctors are arguing that the problems with breathing caused a decline. Hence, this example proves the view about the positive effect renewable energy has on both the environment and the public.

In conclusion, this trend towards renewable energy is a predominantly positive development for the environment. It addresses the depletion of fossil fuels, reduces pollution and carbon emissions, and improves public health. Therefore, governments and individuals should continue investing in green technologies to ensure a sustainable future.

question: These days more people put their personal information, such as names, addresses and telephone numbers, online for everyday activities such as socialising on social networks or banking purposes. Do you think it is a positive or negative development?
essay:
With the rapid growth of digital technology, people increasingly share personal information online for activities such as online banking, shopping, and social networking. Although this trend offers greater convenience and faster access to services, I believe it is largely a negative development because it exposes individuals to serious privacy and security risks.

One major disadvantage is the growing threat of cybercrime. Personal information stored online can be targeted by hackers, leading to identity theft, financial fraud, or unauthorised access to bank accounts. Cybercriminals often use stolen information to make fraudulent transactions or impersonate victims for illegal activities. Even well-established organisations have experienced data breaches, demonstrating that no online system is completely secure. As a result, individuals may suffer significant financial losses as well as emotional distress.

Another concern is the loss of personal privacy. Many websites and mobile applications collect large amounts of user data, including browsing habits, purchasing behaviour, and location history. This information may be shared with third parties for advertising or commercial purposes without users fully understanding how their data will be used. Furthermore, oversharing personal details on social media can expose people to online scams, harassment, or even physical security risks if sensitive information falls into the wrong hands.

Admittedly, storing personal information online has several advantages. It allows users to access banking services, communicate instantly with others, and complete transactions quickly without visiting physical offices. However, these benefits should not outweigh the importance of protecting personal data. Individuals should use strong passwords, enable two-factor authentication, and avoid sharing unnecessary personal information online to reduce potential risks.

In conclusion, although sharing personal information online has made daily life more convenient, I believe it is predominantly a negative development because it increases the risk of cybercrime and threatens individual privacy. As technology continues to evolve, protecting personal information should remain a priority for both governments and individuals.

question: Many companies now allow their staff to work from home for most of the week. Some people think this arrangement benefits employees, while others argue that it harms teamwork and the training of younger staff. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
Home working, which was an emergency measure only a few years ago, has become a permanent arrangement at many firms. Some regard it as a clear improvement in employees' lives, while others believe it undermines collaboration and leaves junior staff without proper training. My own view is that both effects are real, but that they fall on different people.

The benefits to the individual worker are easy to establish. A commute of an hour each way consumes ten hours of an ordinary week, and returning that time to the employee improves sleep, health and family life at no cost to the employer. Home working also removes the low-level interruptions that make concentrated work difficult in an open-plan office, which is why many people report finishing demanding tasks faster at home than in the building they were hired to sit in.

The objection is that the value of an office was never really the desk. Colleagues overhear each other's problems, correct each other's assumptions and pass on judgement that nobody would think to write down. A new graduate learns the unwritten parts of a job by being present while it is done, and scheduled video calls capture almost none of this. Teams also lose the informal contact that resolves small misunderstandings before they become formal disputes.

In my view the arrangement suits experienced staff and disadvantages inexperienced ones. Someone who already knows the work and the people loses very little by leaving the building; someone still learning both loses a great deal. The sensible response is therefore not to choose between the two positions but to apply them differently, requiring far more office attendance in the first years of a career than in the twentieth.

question: Some people believe that newspapers and websites should be free to publish stories about the private lives of famous people. Others think that famous people have the same right to privacy as anyone else. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
The private lives of famous people have always sold newspapers, and online publishing has only increased the appetite for such stories. While I accept that some public figures forfeit part of their privacy, I believe that for most famous people, most of the time, the right to a private life should be protected.

Those who defend intrusive reporting usually make two arguments. The first is that fame is a bargain: actors, athletes and musicians benefit enormously from public attention, and many actively invite it by sharing details of their relationships and homes. It seems inconsistent for them to welcome coverage when it promotes a film and object to it when it reveals a divorce. The second, and stronger, argument concerns people with power. When a politician who campaigns on family values is found to be deceiving his own family, or a minister has undisclosed business interests, the press is exposing hypocrisy or corruption that voters are entitled to know about.

Those who favour stronger protection point out that most celebrity stories involve no such public interest. Photographs of an actor's children on the way to school or reports of a singer's medical treatment tell readers nothing that matters to them; they simply satisfy curiosity. The cost to the person concerned can be severe, since constant pursuit by photographers makes an ordinary life almost impossible, and the harm falls also on relatives who never sought fame at all.

In my view, the second position is more convincing, although the first contains an important exception. Politicians and others who exercise power over the public should expect scrutiny of any private conduct that relates to that power. Entertainers, however, have sold their performances rather than their lives, and publishing their private information purely because readers are curious should not be permitted.

question: Some believe that protecting the environment is the responsibility of individuals, while others think that governments and large companies should take the lead. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay:
It is often argued that protecting the environment is primarily the responsibility of individuals, while others believe that governments and large corporations should take the lead. Although individuals have an important role to play, I believe that governments and major companies have a far greater ability to create meaningful and long-term environmental change.

On the one hand, individuals can contribute significantly to environmental protection through their daily choices. For example, people can reduce their use of plastic, recycle household waste, use public transport and avoid wasting water and electricity. If millions of people adopt these habits, the combined effect can be substantial. Furthermore, individual behaviour can influence businesses, as consumers who prefer environmentally friendly products may encourage companies to adopt greener production methods.

On the other hand, governments and large corporations have much greater resources and influence. Governments can introduce and enforce environmental laws, invest in renewable energy and improve public transport infrastructure. They can also impose taxes or penalties on companies that cause excessive pollution. Large corporations, meanwhile, control huge production and supply chains, meaning that changes in their manufacturing processes can have an impact on millions of consumers. For instance, a major company that replaces fossil fuels with renewable energy across its factories could reduce its carbon emissions on a much larger scale than an individual household ever could.

In my view, environmental protection requires cooperation between individuals, governments and businesses. However, governments and large corporations should take the lead because they have the financial resources, authority and technological capacity to make large-scale changes. Individuals should support these efforts through responsible choices in their everyday lives.

In conclusion, individuals undoubtedly have a responsibility to protect the environment, but governments and large companies are in a much stronger position to tackle environmental problems on a national and global scale. Therefore, I believe that they should take the primary responsibility while encouraging individuals to contribute.

question: Some people believe that the increasing use of technology in education is having a negative impact on students' learning abilities. Others argue that technology is a valuable tool that enhances learning. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
essay:
While it is argued by some people that students’ learning abilities are negatively affected by using modern technology in education, others believe that it can be highly beneficial for the learning process. This essay will discuss both sides of the argument and explain why I support the second view.

There are several reasons why some individuals think that this issue has negative impacts. One of the main reasons is that children put less effort into thinking about complex problems. This means that instead of challenging themselves, they easily use modern devices to clarify the problems, which can have a negative impact on their problem-solving skills in the long term. Another important point is that this matter can reduce the ability of imagination. This is often caused by availibility of applications that provide the details of possible consequences related to a specific problem. For example, a person who must make a decision about an issue based on the possible future effects can use an application to create all the possible consequences without thinking about them.

On the other hand, others believe that this approach is significantly beneficial for the learning process. One major reason for this is that it can make it easier for children to understand complicated problems with visual explanations, which can positively affect the quality of learning. In addition, learning at the individual’s pace is another important factor. If this view is accepted, it is likely to lead to higher levels of productivity and mental well-being. For instance, with the help of modern devices, a student can watch an educational video more than ten times to completely understand a difficult topic.

In conclusion, both sides of the argument have valid reasons. However, I believe that the second approach is more convincing due to factors such as the availability of visual explanations and flexible learning pace.

question: Some people say that technological gadgets like smart phones have made life easier and more convenient. Other people say that they have made life more complex and stressful. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
essay:
Technological gadgets, especially smartphones, have become central to modern life. Some people believe these devices have made daily activities simpler and more convenient, while others argue that they have increased pressure and complexity. In my opinion, smartphones are extremely useful, but they can become stressful when people use them without limits. This essay will discuss both views before explaining why their benefits generally outweigh their disadvantages.

To begin with, smart devices have made many aspects of life easier. For example, people can now communicate instantly, manage bank accounts, book transport, study online, and find directions using one small device. As a result, tasks that once required time, travel, or paperwork can now be completed within minutes. Therefore, gadgets have improved efficiency and given people greater control over their daily routines.

However, these same devices can also make life more demanding. For instance, constant notifications, work emails, social media updates, and online messages can make people feel that they must always be available. Moreover, many users compare their lives with idealised images online, which can increase anxiety and dissatisfaction. Consequently, smartphones may blur the boundary between work and personal life, creating mental pressure instead of freedom.

In conclusion, technological gadgets have brought both convenience and stress to modern society. Nevertheless, I believe they have made life better overall because they save time, improve communication, and expand access to services. People should therefore learn to control their screen time and use technology as a tool rather than allowing it to control their lives.

question: Some people think that advertising is a major factor in driving consumer demand. Others believe that consumers are becoming more immune to advertising. Discuss both views and give your opinion
essay:
Many people argue that advertising is a major contributing factor to consumer demand, while others opine that consumers are becoming less susceptible to such promotional methods. This essay will discuss both views, followed by my personal opinion.

To begin with, advertising can indeed heavily influence consumers' purchasing patterns by introducing new products or services to them and creating product awareness. For instance, a smartphone advertised with more innovative features can prompt buyers to consider upgrading their phones, despite not needing to. Moreover, such promotional methods often include many alluring sounds, colours, and other visual elements, which encourage customers' impulsive decisions when buying the products. Studies have shown that advertising videos for items that contain vibrant hues and strategic editing are directly associated with a higher level of sales.

However, it has also been said that consumers are becoming less likely to fall victim to persuasive advertisements. This could be due to their abundance , as they can be seen everywhere nowadays, from billboards along the roads to local supermarkets. Therefore, people are constantly being exposed to them, to the point where they become less receptive to persuasive messages. In fact, psychology has proven that if one is consistently exposed to certain content, the likelihood of him or her being swayed by it can be reduced. Additionally, negative word-of-mouth can also impact individuals' decisions when buying a product, since it stems from real user experience, and is generally considered more reliable than companies' advertisements, which only focus on creating good publicity.

In conclusion, although consumers are becoming increasingly desensitised towards marketing tactics, advertising still remains an influential component in shaping purchasing decisions. Hence, I believe that its ability to create demand and have an effect on consumers' preferences outweighs the growing immunity towards it. As a result, firms and businesses should continue using advertising strategically by adopting a more personalised approach and addressing specific customer needs and wants.

question: Some people think young people should be free to choose their jobs, but other people think they should be realistic and think more about their future. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay:
Nowadays, choosing the right career decision is one of the most crucial things for young people. Some people believe that they should be free to choose the profession they want, while others argue that they should make a practical career decision based on future employment prospects. This essay will discuss both views before explaining why I think a balance between personal interest and realism is the best approach. 

On the one hand, many people argue that young people should be free to pursue careers that match their interests and passions. Individuals who enjoy their work are generally more motivated, productive and satisfied with their jobs. This often leads to greater professional success and improved mental well-being. Furthermore, allowing young people to choose their preferred careers encourages creativity and innovation. Many successful workers, artists and scientists have achieved remarkable achievements because they followed their passions rather than choosing conventional occupations.

On the other hand, others believe that career decisions should be realistic. Some professions offer limited employment opportunities or low salaries, making it difficult for young people to achieve financial independence. Therefore, choosing a career with strong job prospects, stable income and long-term demand can provide greater economic security and reduce the risk of unemployment. As a result, practical factors such as employability, salary and career progression should not be ignored when selecting an occupation.

To sum up, although young people should be encouraged to follow their ambitions, I believe they should also make realistic career choices by considering future demand and job security. Striking a balance between passion and practicality is the most effective way to achieve long-term career success.

question: Technology has made it possible for people to work from home rather than commuting to an office. Some believe this is a positive development, while others argue it has significant disadvantages. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
The rapid expansion of remote working, accelerated by advances in connectivity software and the widespread disruption of recent years, has prompted legitimate disagreement about its long-term merits. While I recognise the substantial benefits that flexible working arrangements offer, I believe that an exclusively home-based model carries social and professional costs that a well-designed hybrid approach can avoid.

Advocates of remote working point, understandably, to the efficiency gains it delivers. The elimination of daily commutes — which, in many cities, consumes upwards of two hours per day — returns significant time and energy to workers. Additionally, research consistently shows that employees in self-managed environments report lower stress levels and, in many task types, higher output. For knowledge workers in particular, the ability to structure the working day around periods of peak concentration is a genuine productivity advantage.

Those who favour office-based work, however, identify losses that remote arrangements struggle to replicate. Spontaneous professional exchange — the corridor conversation that solves a problem, the informal mentoring that shapes a junior colleague's development — does not transfer easily to a scheduled video call. Furthermore, the boundary between professional and domestic life becomes genuinely difficult to maintain when both occupy the same physical space, a challenge that falls disproportionate on those with caring responsibilities.

My own position is that neither extreme is optimal. A structured hybrid model, where teams meet in person two or three days per week and work remotely for the remainder, preserves the productivity benefits of flexible working while sustaining the social dimension of professional life. The technology that makes remote work possible also makes such coordination straightforward; the question is whether organisations are willing to design it deliberately.
examiner_comment: This is a well-argued essay with a clear, consistent position and strong Coherence at Band 8 — the progression between and within paragraphs is logical and varied, with connectives such as "understandably," "in particular," and "however" used naturally rather than formulaically. The vocabulary range is good, with less common items including "spontaneous professional exchange," "disproportionate," and "self-managed environments." What prevents higher Task Response and Lexical Resource scores is the preposition error "falls disproportionate on" (should be "disproportionately") and the fact that the second body paragraph, while well-structured, would benefit from one more specific example to equal the development of the first. These are characteristic Band 7.5 slips — individually minor, collectively enough to separate this from Band 8+.

question: Some people argue that students should be required to study a broad range of subjects at secondary school, while others believe that young people should focus on the subjects they are most interested in. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
The question of whether secondary schools should offer a broad, compulsory curriculum or allow students to concentrate on subjects that genuinely engage them has long divided educational policymakers. While both positions have considerable merit, I believe that a structured foundation of core subjects, combined with meaningful elective choice, produces the best outcomes for young people.

Those who advocate a wide curriculum argue, with justification, that adolescence is too early for rigid specialisation. Students who have not yet encountered a subject cannot know whether it will ignite a lasting passion or unlock an unexpected aptitude. Moreover, universities and employers consistently value candidates who demonstrate the capacity to think across disciplines — a skill that narrow early specialisation rarely develops. Exposure to history, science, and the arts in parallel encourages the kind of flexible reasoning that proves valuable throughout adult life.

Proponents of student-led choice, however, point to a genuine weakness in compulsory breadth: when students are required to spend years on subjects they find irrelevant, disengagement often follows. Research in educational psychology suggests that intrinsic motivation is among the strongest predictors of academic achievement, and a timetable that ignores student interest risks undermining it. There is also a practical dimension — modern professions demand specialist depth that a generalist secondary education alone cannot provide.

My own view is that these positions are less contradictory than they appear. A core of foundational subjects — literacy, numeracy, and basic scientific understanding — should remain compulsory for all students, as these underpin virtually every career pathway. Beyond this core, structured elective choice allows students' aptitudes and interests to inform their studies without foreclosing essential learning. This hybrid model respects both the value of breadth and the motivating power of personal engagement.
examiner_comment: This is a well-organised essay with a clear, consistent position and a good range of vocabulary including less common items such as "aptitude," "disengagement," and "foreclosing." Coherence is strong at Band 8 — paragraph transitions are natural and varied, and the argument progresses logically without mechanical signposting. What prevents a higher Task Response score is that the second body paragraph's claim about "specialist depth" is asserted rather than illustrated with a concrete example or causal development. The minor ambiguity in "risks undermining it" (where "it" could refer to either motivation or interest) is a characteristic Band 7.5 cohesion slip that slightly weakens the otherwise strong Coherence score.

question: Air travel should be restricted because of pollution and the use of the world’s fuel. Do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is argued that aviation should be limited due to its impact on the environment and the depletion of the world’s fuel resources. I strongly agree with this statement because a significant amount of air travel is unnecessary, and restricting flights could have considerable environmental and economic benefits.

On the one hand, the excessive use of planes should be controlled. Nowadays, wealthy individuals often fly in private jets rather than booking seats on commercial flights, which can transport many people at once. In addition, airlines operate numerous services to short-distance destinations that could easily be reached by car. Therefore, I believe that flying should be reserved for reasonable needs, such as travelling to isolated areas for work, visiting distant family members, or reaching countries that can only be accessed by air. Moreover, governments around the world should regulate aviation to reduce unnecessary journeys. For example, to decrease the number of air trips in the region, the governments of Saudi Arabia, Syria and Turkey could cooperate on a railway project that would allow people to travel between these countries by train.

On the other hand, restricting aviation could make a significant difference to the environment. Planes release enormous amounts of harmful emissions, which contribute to global warming and air pollution. Therefore, reducing the number of flights could help address these environmental problems and support efforts to protect the planet. Furthermore, reducing air travel would conserve fuel resources, as aircraft consume vast quantities of petrol. Excessive consumption could eventually lead to economic difficulties if global fuel production cannot meet demand. For instance, during the Iranian Revolution, a decline in oil exports from the Middle East caused petrol prices to reach historic levels, leading some countries to reduce flights and reserve fuel for more essential purposes, such as electricity generation.

In conclusion, I strongly believe that air transport should be regulated to reduce unnecessary travel. This would help minimise environmental damage while conserving fuel resources and protecting nations from potential fuel-supply emergencies.

question: Some people believe that governments should take responsibility for improving the health of citizens by regulating diet and lifestyle choices, while others think that health is a personal matter and individuals should be free to make their own decisions. To what extent do you agree with the view that governments should intervene in citizens' health choices?
essay:
The appropriate scope of government intervention in individual health choices is a genuinely contested question, made more urgent as rising rates of diet-related illness place growing pressure on public healthcare systems. My view is that governments are justified in regulating industries and environments that shape health outcomes, but that policies restricting personal behaviour cross an important boundary of individual autonomy.
The strongest argument for intervention concerns market failure rather than personal conduct. Left unregulated, food manufacturers have commercial incentives to engineer products that are highly palatable but nutritionally poor, market them aggressively, and price them below healthier alternatives. Governments can legitimately correct this imbalance through nutritional labelling requirements, taxes on high-sugar products, and restrictions on advertising to children — measures that improve the conditions under which individuals choose without dictating the choice itself.
Policies that directly restrict what individuals may eat or how they must live, however, represent a more problematic overreach. Such measures tend to generate resentment and poor compliance, and they concentrate government authority in a domain traditionally reserved for private judgment. Crucially, the harm that an individual's dietary choices causes falls primarily on that individual rather than on others — a distinction that weakens the public-health justification for compulsory restrictions.
In conclusion, governments should intervene assertively in the commercial and structural conditions that shape health, but should stop well short of controlling individual lifestyle choices. The difference between improving the environment of choice and overriding the choice itself is the key boundary that health policy should not cross.
examiner_comment: A well-organised, substantive essay that draws the crucial distinction between regulating industries and restricting individuals — this analytical move elevates the Task Response score. The "market failure" framing in paragraph two is precise and effective; it grounds the argument in a recognisable logical structure rather than mere opinion. Cohesion is managed without mechanical markers; "however" and "crucially" are used sparingly and appropriately. One or two collocations are slightly imprecise ("generates resentment" is natural; "poor compliance" is slightly clinical), but neither impedes meaning. Grammatical range is good; non-finite clauses and passive constructions are used accurately throughout.

question: As we are facing more and more problems, which affect the whole planet, good relationships between different countries are becoming more important than ever before. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is often argued that good relationships between different countries are becoming more important as the world faces an increasing number of global problems. I strongly agree with this view because international cooperation is essential for addressing shared challenges, and it can also promote economic and technological development.

The primary reason why I agree with this view is that many global problems cannot be solved by individual countries. This is mainly because issues such as climate change, pandemics and environmental pollution affect several nations at the same time. In other words, governments need to cooperate by sharing information, technology and resources. For example, countries can work together on renewable energy research, which can reduce dependence on fossil fuels and lower carbon emissions. As a result, strong international relationships can contribute to more effective solutions to global challenges.

Furthermore, another important reason why good international relationships are essential is that they promote economic and technological cooperation. This is because countries can benefit from international trade, foreign investment and knowledge sharing. For instance, universities and research institutions from different countries can cooperate on scientific projects, which may lead to new technologies and practical solutions. Consequently, stronger international ties can create employment opportunities and support long-term economic development. Therefore, I strongly agree that good relationships between countries are more important than ever before.

In conclusion, I firmly agree with the view that good relationships between countries have become increasingly important. This is mainly because international cooperation is necessary to solve global challenges, and it can also support economic and technological development.

question: Both government investment in public transport systems and reductions in public transport ticket prices will help to reduce transport pollution greatly. Do you agree or disagree with this statement? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge and experience.
essay:
Public transportation is a major requirement for metropolises. It is, however, discussed whether government investment and reducing costs are efficient ways to fight against transport pollution. I personally agree that enabling practical public transportation at lower prices for citizens significantly helps with it. In this essay, I will support my statement.

Firstly, new metro lines and bus stops require construction, which mostly takes a large period of time. Furthermore, because of this, many ways and streets are temporarily closed. As a result, traffic increases significantly on a variety of busy roads and highways. For instance, in Barcelona, to arrive at the beach zone, there are common routes not functioning nowadays, which cause traffic congestion due to maintenance in metro line.

On the other hand, lower costs and a large number of subways and coaches encourage people not to drive. To illustrate, tourists and residents in London show a tendency to travel by underground since the London Metro System is one of the most remarkable and enormous examples of all. Another factor is that car parking in London is quite an adverse and pricey issue. Hence, the proportion of private vehicles in traffic is limited in this capital. It is also an advantage that passengers find more flexible, comfortable, and less time-consuming trips.

To sum up, investment in public transport systems and affordable ticket prices are outstanding assets to lessen pollution on city roads. Authorities must plan and schedule renovations and expansions carefully by taking into account peak hours, community routines, and individuals' economic conditions.

question: Many countries spend large amounts of public money on hosting international sporting events. Some people believe that this money is wasted. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Hosting a World Cup or an Olympic Games now costs the host nation billions, and the bill is paid by taxpayers most of whom will never attend an event. I agree that much of this spending is wasted, though I would argue that the waste lies in what gets built rather than in the decision to host.

The strongest case against hosting is the record of what is left behind. Stadiums designed for a fortnight of capacity crowds are handed to cities with no permanent use for them, and their upkeep falls on local budgets for decades afterwards. The promised tourism boom is harder to detect than the bid documents suggest, partly because ordinary visitors avoid a city during the event itself. Money committed to these projects is also money not committed to housing or hospitals, and that trade-off is rarely put to voters in those terms before a bid is submitted.

There are real returns, but they are narrower than supporters claim. Transport links and drainage built for an event outlast it and serve residents afterwards, and a well-run tournament can change how a country is perceived, which has value that is genuine even if it resists measurement. The difficulty is that these gains come from the infrastructure and the organisation rather than from the ceremony, and they can usually be obtained without the ceremony.

My conclusion is that the waste is avoidable rather than inherent. A country that builds only what it would have wanted anyway, and hires venues instead of erecting them, can host well. A country that treats the event as a reason to build monuments is wasting public money, and most hosts, faced with that choice, have chosen the second path.

question: In some countries, there are many social problems involving teenagers. This is because parents spend much of their time at work not at home. Do you agree or disagree?
essay:
There is a common perspective that social problems of young people are caused by a lack of parenting in some states. It has been complained that parents focus on working rather than staying at home. Personally, I totally disagree with this view because I think it is irresponsible to only blame the parents  without figuring out the real reason for the dilemma.

Currently, social obstacles of teenagers have been noticed for a long time , and the reasons are various for each kind of problem. For example, some students intend to bully their classmates in school in order to gain a sense of superiority. These inappropriate behaviours reflect that they were highly likely to be treated in the same way at home.  These kinds of problems caused by terrible parenting should blame their family for sure. Because these behaviours would harm others without correction.

However, on the other hand, certain sorts of issues are not caused by bad parenting. Instead, it might be a result of careless surroundings. For instance, some young children become depressed because they were isolated by peers due to their uncommon selection. This is a systematic problem that needs to be prevented by the institution or the authority. Regulations and policies need to be discussed , and both parents and teachers should be involved to build a healthy system for the children.

In conclusion. I truly believe that certain social issues are caused by a lack of parental accompaniment, but not all of the problems can be blamed on them. It really depends on the initiative of the problem, which is super important to find the reason.

question: Some people think that all advertising aimed at children under the age of twelve should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Children now meet commercial messages in more places than any previous generation, and there are recurring calls to prohibit advertising directed at the under-twelves altogether. I agree with a ban, principally because young children cannot recognise persuasion for what it is, although enforcing one is far harder than the proposal usually admits.

The central argument is about capacity. Advertising is a form of persuasion, and persuasion assumes an audience able to see that someone is trying to change its mind. Children below roughly eight lack that recognition entirely, and even at eleven the understanding is fragile under the pressure of an appealing image. Selling to an audience that cannot tell it is being sold to is not competition but exploitation of a known limitation, and the same reasoning already justifies preventing children from buying alcohol or entering a contract.

A second argument concerns content. The products marketed most heavily to children skew towards confectionery, sugary cereals and fast food, and the cumulative effect on what children come to expect from a meal is well recognised. Restrictions on this category alone have been introduced in several countries.

The difficulty is definitional. A ban on advertising aimed at children is straightforward for a toy commercial in a cartoon break, but far less so for product placement inside a game, a family film sponsored by a brand, or an online personality whose audience happens to be nine. Legislation covering only broadcast advertising simply moves the money online, where oversight is weakest and enforcement slowest.

On balance I support the ban, while recognising that it has to be written in terms of the audience actually reached rather than the audience formally intended. The test of a good rule here is whether a company could comply with its letter while defeating its purpose.

question: When children behave badly, some people believe that their parents rather than their schools should be held responsible. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Children who behave badly are usually a problem for their school before they are a problem for anyone else, which is why schools are so often the first to be blamed. I agree that the primary responsibility lies with parents, but I would distinguish where behaviour originates from who is best placed to change it.

The case for parental responsibility is simply one of time and influence. A child spends its first five years almost entirely at home and learns there what is normal: how disagreements are settled, whether promises are kept, whether adults can be spoken to rudely without consequence. Teachers inherit a child whose expectations have already been formed, and they see that child for a fraction of the week in a group of thirty. Whatever a teacher then attempts has to compete with several years of consistent evidence pointing in the opposite direction. Holding a school accountable for a pattern established before the child arrived is neither fair nor useful.

Schools are not therefore blameless. One with clear rules applied consistently produces better behaviour than one that improvises, and the difference between two schools serving the same neighbourhood is often striking. What a school can do, however, is contain and redirect behaviour rather than originate it, and a teacher trying to compensate for what happens at home is working against the clock.

My position is that parents should answer for how a child behaves and schools for how they respond to it. Blaming teachers for the first is a way of avoiding a conversation nobody wants to have with parents, and it leaves the actual cause untouched. It also asks the wrong institution to solve a problem it did not create.
